title: How to Send Money from Ethiopia to China
summary: Sending money from Ethiopia to China is slow if you rely on banks alone. Here's what actually works for Ethiopian businesses and individuals paying Chinese suppliers.
body_text: I've talked to enough Ethiopian importers to know what the payment process usually looks like. You have a supplier in Guangzhou or Yiwu. You have a commercial invoice and agreed delivery terms. And then the real work starts: figuring out how to actually get the money from Addis Ababa to a Chinese bank account without it disappearing into a foreign exchange queue for two months. China is Ethiopia's largest trading partner. Ethiopia brings in machinery, electronics, building materials, and consumer goods from Chinese manufacturers at a scale that puts this corridor among the most active on the continent. Bilateral trade has exceeded three billion dollars annually, and the relationship has deepened steadily through infrastructure investment and manufacturing partnerships under the Belt and Road Initiative. What the trade data doesn't capture is how hard the payment leg of that relationship can be. The route from birr to yuan has real structural challenges, and knowing what they are before you try to move money will save you a lot of frustration. Why the forex situation matters to you specifically The National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE) maintains foreign exchange controls that shape every outbound transfer from the country. The Ethiopian birr is not freely convertible. When a business wants to pay a Chinese supplier in US dollars or yuan, it needs to go through its commercial bank and apply for a foreign exchange allocation. Priority goes to essential imports: petroleum, pharmaceuticals, certain food products. Everything else joins a queue. For importers in fashion, electronics, building materials, or consumer goods, this creates a practical timing problem. Your supplier quoted a price. You agreed on delivery. But by the time the FX allocation clears, the birr has moved, your cost calculations are off, and your supplier has sent three unanswered messages on WeChat wondering what happened to the wire. The wait can stretch from weeks to months depending on your sector, your bank relationship, and the overall pressure on Ethiopia's foreign reserves at that moment. Nigeria has had its own version of this problem. The difference with Ethiopia is that the controls sit closer to the top of the transaction, so there are fewer informal channels and more formal ones that you actually need to understand. The mistake most Ethiopian importers make Most businesses I've watched approach this corridor treat it as a banking problem. They go to Commercial Bank of Ethiopia, Dashen Bank, or Awash Bank, submit the required paperwork, and wait. When things slow down, they escalate. When that doesn't help, they call someone who promises to move things faster. The issue isn't which bank you use. Your bank isn't slow because it's inefficient. It's operating under the same foreign exchange constraints as every other commercial bank in Ethiopia. Switching institutions rarely solves the core problem. What changes your outcome is understanding which payment channels work for which transaction types, structuring your imports to match the channels that are actually available to you, and knowing the documentation requirements before a compliance flag shows up and stalls a transfer that was already in motion. Four channels worth knowing Bank wire transfers via SWIFT are still the backbone of commercial payments out of Ethiopia. CBE, Dashen, Awash, and Wegagen Bank all offer outbound international wire services. The process requires documentation: commercial invoice, purchase order, and import permit where applicable. NBE priority FX allocations go to certain sectors. If your business imports fall into a priority category, bank wires can move faster than you might expect. If they don't, the queue is real and planning around it is more useful than fighting it. Licensed money transfer operators are a second channel. Ethiopia authorizes a set of International Money Transfer Operators to operate in the country, including Western Union and MoneyGram. These work well for personal transfers and smaller amounts. Business payment limits are tighter, and the same documentation requirements apply. Digital transfer platforms are where I'd point most small and mid-sized Ethiopian importers right now. Mobile-first apps that connect into international payment rails are increasingly available in the Ethiopian market, and the practical advantage they offer is real: they aggregate foreign exchange capacity across multiple sources rather than drawing from a single bank's allocation under NBE constraints. That flexibility can meaningfully change the timeline. Afriex supports the Ethiopia-to-China corridor, though I'd encourage you to compare options and verify what's currently available for your specific transaction size and purpose. Rates, limits, and processing times vary, and the only honest way to compare is to look at end-to-end cost on a specific amount, not just the headline fee. For larger importers moving high volumes per shipment, Letters of Credit are worth understanding. Ethiopian commercial banks offer LC facilities, and Chinese suppliers who've worked with African buyers understand how to receive them. The setup overhead isn't worth it for small or one-off transactions, but for businesses running consistent high-volume import cycles, LCs can reduce supplier friction significantly and sometimes unlock better payment terms from the Chinese side. What to have ready before you initiate a transfer Chinese banks are specific about incoming wire details. A small error on beneficiary information causes a return transfer, which means delays, additional fees, and an unhappy supplier. Before you initiate anything, get the following from your supplier in writing: The full legal name of the bank, not a nickname or abbreviation. The branch name and address. The account number as it appears on the account. The SWIFT/BIC code for the bank. The beneficiary name exactly as it appears on the bank account. For amounts above a certain threshold, your bank or platform may also require the purpose of payment. Stating "payment for goods under contract reference [number] per attached commercial invoice" is a clean statement that moves through compliance review without triggering unnecessary flags. Keep your commercial invoice and purchase order on hand during the transfer process. Some platforms request these upfront as part of onboarding or transaction initiation. Others only ask when a compliance review is triggered on the back end. Either way, having them ready means you're not hunting for documents when the clock is running. One additional thing: verify that your Chinese supplier's bank can receive international wires directly. Some smaller regional Chinese banks route incoming foreign wires through correspondent banks, which can add a day or two to settlement. Asking your supplier which bank they use, and whether they've received international transfers to that account before, is a five-minute conversation that can save you a week of confusion. Working out what you're actually paying Ethiopia-to-China transfers typically involve two currency conversions: birr to US dollars, then US dollars to Chinese yuan. Each step carries a margin, and not all platforms show you both margins transparently when they present their rates. My approach when evaluating any transfer option is to calculate end-to-end. What does 500,000 ETB become, in yuan, by the time it hits the recipient account? That final number, compared across platforms and against the interbank rate for both pairs, tells you the real cost of the transfer. The headline "zero fees" or "low fees" claim on its own tells you very little. The NBE publishes its daily reference exchange rate for the birr. The People's Bank of China publishes daily rates for the yuan. Use both as reference points when you compare platform quotes. You may not get the interbank rate on either conversion, but you should know how far off it you are. A shift happening across the region Kenya finalized its Virtual Asset Service Provider regulations in July 2026, completing a licensing framework for all digital financial platforms operating in the country. I've been watching developments like this across East Africa, not because stablecoin regulation is directly relevant to most Ethiopian importers paying Chinese suppliers today, but because these regulatory frameworks shape which platforms can operate and how reliably they can serve you over time. Ethiopia's NBE has moved more conservatively than its East African peers on digital payment licensing. But the direction of travel across the region is toward more structured and formalized digital transfer ecosystems, not less. Platforms that have been navigating regulatory complexity in multiple African markets are building the compliance infrastructure that will make them more reliable over a three to five year horizon. For Ethiopian businesses planning their payment infrastructure with any foresight, understanding the digital transfer landscape now is better than being forced to learn it quickly when a bank wire is stuck and you're looking for alternatives under pressure. If you're sending as an individual If your situation is a personal transfer rather than a business payment, the practical dynamics are different. You're not dealing with FX allocation queues for import licenses. The channels available to you are licensed MTOs and digital transfer platforms, and both work reasonably well at personal transfer volumes. What matters most: verify the platform you use is authorized to operate in Ethiopia. Check the rate you're being quoted against the NBE's published rate for the birr. Confirm the transfer method your recipient prefers. Chinese bank accounts can receive international wires with the standard beneficiary details. If your recipient wants funds into Alipay or WeChat Pay instead, check with them about whether their setup can accept international transfers, because some configurations of those accounts don't support inbound international transfers without specific settings enabled. The short version The Ethiopia-China corridor is not effortless to navigate, and I won't pretend otherwise. Foreign exchange controls are real, documentation requirements are strict, and the timeline for commercial bank wires can test your supplier relationships. But the options available today are genuinely better than they were three years ago. Digital platforms have expanded into the Ethiopian market. Licensed operators are functioning. The trade relationship is large enough that banks and platforms on both sides have real experience with these flows. We built Afriex to be a usable option for corridors like this, though I'd always encourage you to compare it against other services and check what's available for your transaction type and volume. What matters most is that you know what rate you're getting before you send, what timeline to communicate to your supplier, and what documentation you're keeping on your side of the transaction. The next time your Chinese supplier asks when the payment will arrive, you should be able to answer with a specific number of business days, not "I'm still waiting on the bank."

body_text: Award Advances U.S. Air Force Global Strike Command’s Layered Base Defense While Cementing Titan as a Global Benchmark in Counter-UAS ARLINGTON, Va. — July 7, 2026 — AeroVironment, Inc. (“AV”) (NASDAQ: AVAV), a global leader in intelligent, multi-domain robotic systems, today announced that Joint Interagency Task Force 401 (JIATF-401) has selected its Titan™ MS (Multi-Sensor) system for a $80.5 million contract award in support of Domestic Shield. The award is being executed against a $500 million Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) sole-source contract in support of Joint Interagency Task Force 401’s (JIATF-401) Domestic Shield Program that was recently announced by AV . “JIATF-401 is continuously working to bolster the Services’ abilities to protect warfighters and individual installations,” said Col. Jason Idleman, Chief for Multi-Domain Operations Division at JIATF-401. “This investment provides operators with the tools to detect, track, and defend against illicit drones. Providing top-tier technology to our warfighters enables them to effectively respond to these rapidly evolving threats.” Domestic Shield is the Department of War’s initiative to strengthen C-UAS protection for defense critical infrastructure and other high-priority homeland defense. JIATF 401 spearheads the initiative by prioritizing sites based on threat, criticality, vulnerability, and mission. The task force works with the Services and interagency partners to validate requirements, align resources, and accelerate the delivery of layered C-UAS capabilities to the locations where they are needed most. Under this purchase order, AV will deliver Titan systems that will enhance the Air Force’s layered air defense capabilities against small unmanned aircraft system (sUAS) threats. This award follows a previous JIATF-401 purchase of a Titan C-UAS system . “Counter-UAS is no longer a future requirement, it is the defining operational imperative of modern defense,” said Wahid Nawabi, Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer at AV. “This milestone award and the unprecedented demand we are seeing for Titan mark a historic turning point, as customers move decisively toward proven, fielded solutions that can be rapidly deployed at scale to protect civilians, servicemembers and critical assets against increasingly sophisticated drone threats.” Titan-MS is an AI-powered, multi-sensor fusion solution that detects, identifies, tracks, defeats and reports on unmanned system threats. A multi-mission, multi-threat solution suitable for air, sea and land environments, Titan MS fuses AI and machine learning algorithms from industry-leading sensors to counter both RF-controlled and autonomous drone threats. Titan products are currently integrated in multiple programs of record within the U.S. Department of War, other U.S. government agencies and international partners. “We continue to refine our software-defined Titan family based on direct customer feedback and hard-earned lessons from combat operations, ensuring our capabilities evolve faster than the threats and keep our customers decisively ahead,” said Trace Stevenson, President of Autonomous Systems at AV. “This JIATF-401 award underscores Titan’s ability to deliver mission-ready performance at scale for some of the most demanding base defense environments in the world.” Titan™ Family Momentum The Titan family, including Titan3™, Titan4™ and Titan-SV™, is a modular suite of C-UAS solutions that detect, identify, track and mitigate hostile or unauthorized drones across diverse environments. Titan products are integrated in multiple programs of record within the U.S. Department of War, other U.S. government agencies and international partners. During the quarter, AV delivered 118 Titan 4 systems and 400 Titan-SV systems worldwide, signaling Titan as a benchmark for market adoption in advanced C-UAS solutions protecting critical locations and high-profile events. Titan is operationally deployed in 17 countries worldwide, including three new international customers fielding the system this quarter. Demand for Titan systems is accelerating as federal, state and local agencies move quickly to address the proliferation of sophisticated unmanned threats. Recent federal policy changes, including the President’s Executive Order “Restoring American Airspace Sovereignty” and the SAFER SKIES Act , are further enabling broader deployment of compliant, mission-ready counter-drone capabilities. AV’s Titan family is designed and manufactured to meet U.S. regulatory requirements, providing customers with confidence in both operational performance and compliance. Titan’s architecture supports continuous evolution to meet rapidly advancing threats. In 2025, AV introduced Titan4, a highly portable variant for mobile, dismounted or fixed-site operations. Deployable in under five minutes, Titan4 creates a protective “dome” around personnel and infrastructure. Its single compact chassis is 17% lighter and 73% smaller than its predecessor, delivering nearly 250% more transmit power, with 540W output across six RF bands to address evolving threats, integrated with Titan-SV for AI-enabled passive precision detection and airspace awareness. More about Titan Products About AV AeroVironment (“AV”) (NASDAQ: AVAV) is a defense technology leader delivering integrated capabilities across air, land, sea, space, and cyber. The Company develops and deploys autonomous systems, loitering munitions, counter-UAS technologies, space-based platforms, directed energy systems, and cyber and electronic warfare capabilities—built to meet the mission needs of today’s warfighter and tomorrow’s conflicts. At the core of these technologies lies AV_Halo™, a modular, mission-ready suite of AI-powered software tools that empowers warfighters and enables full-battlefield dominance: detect, decide, deliver. With a national manufacturing footprint and a deep innovation pipeline, AV delivers proven systems and future-defining capabilities at speed, scale, and operational relevance. For more information, visit www.avinc.com . title: Dental Supply Procurement Software Comparison 2026
body_text: The best dental supply procurement software in 2026 are Alara (free, multi-vendor price comparison), ZenOne ($49/month, AI price optimization for independent practices), Torch Dental (pricing on request, curated AI-guided vendor network), Method USA (barcode-driven inventory automation), Dentira (enterprise DSO source-to-pay), and CureMint (ERP-integrated group spend management). Each platform targets a different practice size and procurement complexity the right choice depends on your location count, PMS, and whether pricing transparency or inventory automation is your biggest gap. Dental supply costs have risen 34% since 2020. Ninety percent of dentists reported additional increases in H1 2025 alone, according to ADA Health Policy Institute data. Yet most practices are still managing procurement the same way they did a decade ago: one supplier, a clipboard, and whoever has time to make the call. The average dental practice spends 7.2% of collections on supplies, well above the ADA benchmark of 5–6%. For a practice collecting $1 million annually, that gap represents $12,000 to $22,000 in avoidable annual excess before a single staff hour spent on vendor calls and invoice reconciliation is counted. This guide compares the top dental supply procurement software platforms in 2026, from free price-comparison tools to enterprise DSO procurement systems. You'll see what each platform costs, what it actually does, and which approach fits your practice size and procurement complexity. Key Takeaways: Arini's 2026 Dental Procurement Analysis The average dental practice spends 7.2% of collections on supplies 1–2 percentage points above the ADA benchmark of 5–6%, representing $10,000–$20,000 in avoidable excess per million in collections. Conservative estimates put manual procurement waste at $15,000–$25,000 per year for a single-location practice, from duplicate orders, missed vendor pricing, and staff hours spent on purchasing tasks. Practices that switch to automated procurement systems have reduced monthly supply spending by $8,000–$10,000 in the first four months, according to Dental Economics . AI-powered procurement platforms that forecast needs based on scheduled procedure volume prevent both overstocking and mid-week shortages the two most expensive supply management failure modes. Dental supply procurement software does not replace your PMS it integrates with it. Deep integrations with OpenDental, EagleSoft, and Denticon are the baseline expectation in 2026, not a premium feature. Procurement software handles the supply-spend side of dental operations. Practices seeing the strongest financial outcomes pair procurement tools with an AI receptionist like Arini that captures missed production on the revenue side. What Is Dental Supply Procurement Software? Dental supply procurement software is a platform that centralizes and automates the purchasing lifecycle for dental consumables, equipment, and office supplies. Instead of one staff member calling a rep, another checking inventory on a clipboard, and a third manually entering invoices, a procurement platform handles all three and connects the workflow to your practice management system. The category spans a wide range of capabilities. At the basic end, standalone dental supply management software gives you a digital catalog and approval workflows. At the advanced end, AI-powered systems forecast reorder needs based on scheduled procedures, surface real-time price comparisons across multiple vendors, and flag spend anomalies before they hit your P&L. For dental groups and DSOs , procurement software solves an additional problem: standardization across locations. Without a shared system, practices within the same group order the same supplies from different vendors at different prices a visibility problem that compounds with every location added. The Dental Practice Management Software Market is projected, according to Mordor Intelligence , to grow from $2.62 billion in 2026 to $4.44 billion by 2031, driven largely by operational automation tools including procurement and inventory management. The shift from spreadsheet-based ordering to software-driven procurement is no longer a competitive differentiator it's becoming table stakes for practices managing more than $500,000 in annual collections. Why Dental Practices Are Rethinking Supply Procurement Three factors are pushing practices away from manual ordering in 2026: Supply cost inflation. Supply costs have risen 34% since 2020 and 90% of dentists reported continued increases in H1 2025 alone. "We've always ordered from the same rep" is an increasingly expensive default when the same consumable can vary 20–40% in price across the full vendor marketplace. Single-distributor dependency. Most practices default to one primary supplier out of habit or rep relationships. Multi-vendor price comparison automatic on procurement software, impossible manually is where the documented 15–17% annual savings comes from. A practice spending $60,000 per year on supplies captures $9,000–$10,200 annually from automated price comparison alone. The only way to surface that savings opportunity is to move from single-vendor ordering to a procurement platform that queries multiple suppliers on every order. Staff time reallocation. The average office manager spends 3–5 hours per week on purchasing tasks. At $25–$35/hour, that's $3,900–$9,100 in annual labor cost going to a process that software handles in minutes. The most efficient practices have eliminated manual purchasing entirely by shifting to automated reorder workflows. For multi-location groups, multiply that by every location. The Hidden Cost of Manual Dental Procurement Manual procurement looks cheap because the upfront cost is zero. The actual cost shows up elsewhere. Staff time. The average dental office manager spends 3–5 hours per week on supply purchasing, vendor calls, invoice reconciliation, and inventory checks. At $25–$35 per hour, that's $3,900–$9,100 per year on a task that software can handle in minutes. Duplicate orders. Without centralized inventory visibility, practices routinely order products already in stock. Expired products go unnoticed until a procedural moment then get written off. Method Procurement estimates all-in waste for a single-location practice at $15,000–$25,000 per year when you account for duplicate ordering, expired inventory, and non-competitive vendor pricing. No price visibility. Most dental practices order from a single primary supplier out of habit or convenience. Across multiple vendors, the same consumable can vary 20–40% in price. Manual ordering gives you no way to surface those gaps without calling multiple reps and manually comparing quotes. No spend accountability. When purchasing is done by whoever is available, there's no audit trail, no approval routing, and no budget enforcement. When supply costs creep above the 5–6% ADA benchmark, practice owners often find out at year-end long after the opportunity to correct course. For multi-location practices and DSOs, manual procurement scales these problems linearly. Each location develops its own ordering habits, vendor relationships, and product preferences. The result is fragmented spend that's impossible to benchmark, negotiate, or standardize. Dental Procurement Software: Feature-by-Feature Comparison This dental procurement software comparison covers the three primary approaches to dental supply procurement in 2026. Use it as a decision framework rather than a rigid ranking the right approach depends on your practice size, PMS, and procurement complexity. Core purchasing and inventory features: Procurement Solutions Comparison Feature Manual / Spreadsheet Basic Procurement Software AI-Powered Procurement Vendor price comparison None; one vendor per order Limited, manual queries Automated across 200+ vendors in real time Inventory tracking Clipboard or manual spreadsheet Basic par-level alerts Predictive restocking based on scheduled procedure volume Order approval workflow Email or phone chain Digital approvals with basic routing Automated with budget controls and role-based spend caps PMS integration None Select platforms, limited depth Deep integration (OpenDental, EagleSoft, Denticon) Multi-location support Impossible to standardize Limited cross-site visibility Centralized dashboard with cross-location spend analytics Invoice reconciliation Manual line-by-line Semi-automated matching Fully automated with discrepancy flagging Financial controls and administration: Procurement Management Features Comparison Feature Manual / Spreadsheet Basic Procurement Software AI-Powered Procurement Formulary management Ad hoc preferred vendor list Basic approved vendor catalog AI-driven formulary with compliance and substitution tracking Spend analytics and reporting None or manual Excel Basic monthly spend reports Real-time dashboards with category-level and location-level analysis Budget enforcement None Soft spend limits Hard budget caps with automated escalation Expiration tracking Reactive (caught when needed) Basic email alerts Proactive alerts with automated waste reduction recommendations Supplier relationship management Phone and email per rep Vendor portal access Automated ordering with supplier performance tracking Setup and onboarding None required Days to weeks Dedicated implementation support and training The Tier That Actually Moves the Needle Basic procurement software solves the workflow problem you get digital purchase orders, approval chains, and some inventory visibility. But it doesn't solve the pricing problem or the forecasting problem. You still order reactively, you still miss price drops across vendors, and you still rely on staff judgment for reorder timing. AI-powered procurement platforms add two capabilities that change the economics meaningfully: Real-time price comparison across the full vendor marketplace so every order automatically surfaces the best available price, not just the price from your habitual supplier. Procedure-linked forecasting so the platform can predict what you'll need next week based on what's scheduled, not what ran out today. A 55-location orthodontic and pediatric dental organization cited in procurement industry case studies achieved a 20% reduction in supply costs and 50% decrease in procurement time after switching from manual purchasing to an automated procurement platform. For a DSO that size, that's hundreds of thousands of dollars per year in recovered margin. What to Look for in Dental Supply Procurement Software Not all procurement platforms are built for dental. General-purpose spend management tools often lack the vendor integrations, clinical product taxonomies, and PMS connections that dental practices need. When evaluating options in 2026, these are the dimensions that separate functional from excellent: PMS Integration Depth A procurement platform should pull scheduled procedure data from your PMS to forecast supply needs, and push order confirmations and invoice data back into your financial records. Confirm native support for your specific PMS OpenDental, EagleSoft , Denticon, or CareStack and ask whether integration requires a third-party connector or middleware. Vendor Network Coverage The value of real-time price comparison is directly proportional to how many vendors the platform connects to. Platforms with access to 13+ major dental distributors surface pricing variations that single-vendor ordering never reveals. Ask vendors for specifics on distributor partnerships before committing. Budget Controls and Approval Workflows For multi-location practices, the ability to set location-level spend budgets, require manager approval above a threshold, and enforce a preferred formulary is not optional it's how you prevent one location's purchasing habits from undermining group-wide margins. Spend Analytics and Benchmarking The best platforms give you not just what you spent, but how your spend compares to benchmarks for your practice type. Knowing you're at 7.8% of collections on supplies is actionable. Knowing the benchmark for a three-chair single-location practice is 5.2% turns that number into a specific savings target. Implementation and Ongoing Support Procurement software adds value only when staff use it consistently. Platforms that offer dedicated onboarding support, training materials for front-desk and clinical staff, and responsive support during the transition period deliver faster time-to-value than self-serve platforms with minimal guidance. Top Dental Supply Procurement Software Platforms in 2026 The best dental supply procurement software platforms in 2026: ZenOne ($49/month) - AI price comparison across 170+ suppliers, no-contract flexibility for independent practices Torch Dental (pricing on request) - AI-guided recommendations with curated 50+ vendor network and dedicated support Alara (free) - Multi-vendor price comparison layered on top of existing distributor accounts Method USA (custom pricing) - Barcode-driven inventory automation for high-volume and multi-location practices Dentira (enterprise) - AI and RPA-driven source-to-pay platform for DSOs managing 20+ locations CureMint (custom pricing) - ERP-integrated spend management with NetSuite, QuickBooks, and Sage Intacct connectivity The dental supply procurement market includes platforms across three categories: AI-powered price optimization tools for independent practices, barcode-driven inventory systems, and enterprise DSO platforms. Here is how the major options compare. 1. ZenOne Best for Price Transparency and Flexibility ZenOne is the most flexible dental supply procurement software for independent practices, combining AI price comparison with a no-contract, month-to-month model no other platform at this price point offers. It connects dental practices to 170+ suppliers with AI-powered price comparison that surfaces the lowest available price without supplier commissions or loyalty program bias. The platform is vendor-neutral by design unlike platforms that curate networks around preferred distributor relationships. ZenOne customers average $17,000 in annual supply savings, and the platform holds a 5.0 Google rating across its user base. Key Features Access to 170+ suppliers with unbiased AI price comparison QR code and barcode inventory management Budget tracking and spend analytics Month-to-month contracts cancel at any time Pricing: $49/month no contract required Best For: Independent practices and small groups prioritizing price transparency and vendor-neutral access to the full supply marketplace without long-term commitment. 2. Torch Dental Best for Managed AI Procurement Torch Dental is the leading dental supply platform for practices that want dedicated procurement support, serving 3,000+ dental practices with an AI-powered recommendation engine and a curated catalog of 50+ authorized suppliers and 100,000+ SKUs. Dedicated support from ex-dental industry experts differentiates the platform for practices new to digital procurement. Commack Hills Dental Group documented 26% savings on supply ordering after switching to Torch. Key Features AI-powered supply recommendations Curated vendor network (50+ authorized suppliers, 100,000+ SKUs) Budget dashboards and consolidated multi-supplier ordering Expert procurement support and dedicated guidance Pricing: Custom pricing contact for quote Best For: Independent practices and small groups that want AI-guided procurement and are comfortable with a curated vendor catalog and a contract commitment in exchange for managed support. 3. Alara Best Free Multi-Vendor Price Comparison Alara is a free dental supply procurement platform that connects to existing vendor accounts Patterson, Henry Schein, Benco, Darby and surfaces side-by-side pricing across all of them in a single view. No supplier switching is required. Alara layers price comparison on top of current relationships, with revenue coming from the supplier side rather than from practices. Key Features Side-by-side pricing across existing vendor accounts AI-powered product equivalency identification for generic substitutions Single-cart ordering across multiple suppliers Peer reviews and verified product listings Pricing: Free for dental practices Best For: Cost-conscious single-location practices looking to add vendor price comparison immediately with no upfront investment and no disruption to existing supplier relationships. 4. Method USA Best Barcode-Driven Inventory Automation Method USA is the leading barcode-driven dental inventory platform for high-volume practices where physical stock counting is the primary operational bottleneck. It automates stock level tracking through barcode scanning staff scan supplies as they're used, and the platform recalculates reorder needs automatically without manual counts. The interface is designed for non-technical dental teams. Method USA has documented 30–40% savings on supply costs for practices transitioning from manual ordering. Key Features Barcode scanning for automatic inventory level updates Centralized multi-location purchasing dashboard Real-time pricing and order approval workflows Staff-friendly interface designed for non-technical teams Pricing: Custom quote-based (varies by number of locations) Best For: Practices where physical inventory tracking is the primary bottleneck particularly large-team or high-volume locations where manual counting is a consistent operational failure point. 5. Dentira Best Enterprise Procurement Platform for DSOs Dentira serves 8,000+ dental practices and 200+ DSOs with AI and RPA-driven source-to-pay automation. The platform handles ordering, invoicing, and catalog management at enterprise scale, with notable deployments at Heartland Dental and Affordable Care. For DSOs managing 20+ locations, Dentira provides the governance layers and distributor integrations that general-purpose procurement tools cannot replicate. Key Features AI and RPA-driven source-to-pay automation Real-time pricing and catalog management across major dental distributors Full DSO procurement governance with approval hierarchies Enterprise-grade reporting and compliance tracking Pricing: Enterprise custom pricing contact for quote Best For: DSOs and large multi-location groups (20+ locations) that need enterprise-grade procurement governance, deep distributor integrations, and full source-to-payment automation at scale. 6. CureMint Best for ERP-Integrated Spend Visibility CureMint is a vendor-agnostic spend management and procurement platform built for dental groups and DSOs. InterDent selected CureMint to power its clinical supply chain, according to Group Dentistry Now . The platform's strongest differentiator is financial system integration connecting to NetSuite, QuickBooks, and Sage Intacct for automated accounts payable workflows alongside procurement. Key Features Vendor-agnostic multi-supplier ordering in a single interface Real-time spend tracking across all locations Budget monitoring and automated purchasing lists Financial systems integration (NetSuite, QuickBooks, Sage Intacct) Pricing: Custom quote-based pricing Best For: Multi-location dental groups and DSOs where ERP and accounting system integration is as critical as supply ordering particularly organizations where AP automation is part of the procurement goal. AI vs. Basic Dental Procurement: What the Gap Looks Like Practices sometimes evaluate procurement software based on the lowest price point that checks the "we have a system" box. The problem is that basic software addresses the process problem without addressing the pricing and forecasting problem which is where the real money is. The pricing gap. Basic procurement software typically lets you order through a digital portal from your existing supplier relationships. It doesn't automatically query the full vendor marketplace on every order. Practices that add real-time price comparison typically save 15–17% annually without changing clinical protocols or supplier quality, according to Torch Dental , which reports an average of 16% savings for practices on the platform. The forecasting gap. Manual reorder triggers whether physical par levels or calendar reminders are reactive. You notice you're low when a staff member checks the cabinet. AI-powered platforms forecast by pulling your scheduled procedure list from the PMS, calculating the supplies needed for those procedures, and generating purchase recommendations before anything runs out. title: FlowEQ (Production)
body_text: In a survey conducted by Zendesk, 92% of executives say they’ve had to rethink how they work because of the pandemic. Leadership is reconsidering how they structure workflows and engage employees. But what does this trend mean for customer service teams? A cohesive workflow for your customer support team is important for everyone: team members, the company at large, and, of course, the customer. A dysfunctional process likely means unhappy clientele and a loss of revenue . By incorporating a process improvement methodology, customer support teams can continuously provide value while remaining flexible to change. ‍ What are Process Improvement Methodologies? Process improvement methodologies are strategies that lay the foundation for the way teams structure their operations. Some of these frameworks are more philosophical while others require a step-by-step approach. With so many options available to explore, how do you know which ones are best suited for your teams and the customers they aim to support? To answer this question, let’s dive into what process outcomes customer service teams should expect. Benchmarks include: Increased retention Reduced churn Continuous growth Measurable customer satisfaction To meet these objectives, look for processes that promote collaboration between teams, clear communication, and access to information. Here are three process improvement methodologies that do just that. ‍ 1. DMADV: Establish or Strengthen Your Customer Experience Six Sigma’s DMADV is a leading process framework for support professionals that can improve every aspect of their customer service. Use this five-step protocol to create goals around improving your customer experience. Each one should be backed by data and customer feedback. Define: Understand the value your customers expect from your product or service. Generate feedback from your team about common pitfalls that make it difficult to deliver that value. Maybe your team excels at resolving tickets, but the issues creating the tickets get no attention. Measure: Track metrics and customer feedback surrounding your product or service. Customer reviews, web analytics, and feedback from your team can all be used to develop a deeper understanding of how you can deliver value. Analyze: After acquiring metrics, find opportunities for improvement. Maybe there’s a pattern that surfaces or a new-found reason customers are churning. Design: Informed by the previous steps, create a workflow aimed at delivering the value your customers want. It could be as simple as creating an FAQ webpage or changing your company’s billing structure. Verify: Pilot your new process, examine the outcome, and make final adjustments. Keep your ear to the ground by staying sensitive to customer feedback. Are they applauding your changes or creating even more tickets? DMADV is a proven option, but it’s not an overnight savior. Only pursue DMADV If you have 6+ months to dedicate to customer research and product improvements. If you need to make big changes quickly, consider the following methodologies. ‍ 2. Lean Thinking: Remove Bottlenecks and Inefficiencies The main goal of the Lean methodology is getting rid of inefficiencies while creating more value for customers. DMADV is best used to remove defects from your process, while Lean focuses on getting value to your customers as fast as possible. Although Lean is more of a mindset than a protocol, it’s usually implemented in five stages. Specify value: This step is meant to uncover what customers want and why they turn to you to get it. Once you know what value you hope to provide, pinpoint what's preventing it from reaching the customer. Customer surveys, web analytics, and product data will help you figure this out. Map: First, create a map of your current process—the one you want to fix. What steps do team members take, and where are the roadblocks? Maybe the new chatbot on your website is actually causing more tickets than it’s resolving? Look for opportunities to remove or condense steps to help the customer as quickly as possible. Flow: Now that you’ve eliminated unnecessary steps, you should have a simple overview of how you’re delivering what’s important to your customer—this is called your value stream. Put your process map in action and physically follow the “flow” in real time. Pull: Since you’ve shaved off unnecessary energy, you can deliver your company’s value faster. As a result, products and services don’t need to be prepared in excess or ahead of time. Since you removed that chatbot, you can reallocate time and effort to your customers. Perfection: With the root causes of your problems eliminated, this is the time for polishing. Revisit each step until you’ve created a streamlined process. Although the goal of Lean is to remove inefficiencies from your team’s process, it’s always important to remember how changes affect your customers. What may be more efficient for your team isn’t always aligned with the customer experience. ‍ 3. Kaizen: Align Siloed Teams and Their Purpose Similar to Lean, Kaizen is more of an ethos than an actionable strategy. Rooted in Japanese culture and business, its main principle is continuous improvement. Because Kaizen is an idea, there’s really no specific tool or template to start with. One way to fold Kaizen into your process improvement goals is by hosting Kaizen events . Think of Kaizen events as brainstorming sessions or open forums that bring all your teams together. Kick off a Kaizen event with each team that will be affected by any changes: customer support, product development, IT, and sales. The goal is to solve problems through groupthink. By collecting feedback from across the business, a holistic perspective of what’s happening is sure to surface. After a Kaizen event, perhaps the product team learned about a hidden UX bug. After correcting the issue, that never-ending backlog of support tickets was cut in half. For more in-depth process challenges, consider hosting multi-day Kaizen events to bring together siloed teams and promote collaboration. ‍ Take an “À La Carte” Approach to Process Methodologies With so many methods to choose from, deciding which option is best for your customer service team is certainly a challenge. Our advice? Consider these options as beginning frameworks, not finite blueprints. Make them your own by taking pieces from all of them, and reject what doesn’t line up with your customer’s expectations. Regardless of which approach you pursue, your customer should remain at the forefront of all decisions. The days of fixing a process solely for cost reduction and efficiency are gone. Place the customer at the center of everything, and the rest will follow.

title: How Employment Hero Reimagined Mental Health Support for High Performers
summary: Employment Hero, the leading HR and payroll software for Australian SMEs, operates a high performance culture that celebrates ambition. They recognized a critical gap: they were treating mental health as separate from performance, rather than central to it.
body_text: The Problem Employment Hero’s 1,800+ “Heroes” operate in a remote first, globally distributed environment, where managers could see obvious distress but often missed the subtler warning signs along the way. High performers tend to absorb stress silently until they hit a breaking point, and without a structured way to catch emerging psychosocial risks early, the organisation was stuck reacting to burnout only after it had already caused harm. Their existing EAP wasn’t helping: utilisation sat at just 7%, it stayed passive in the background until a crisis hit, and it offered no real visibility into workplace stress or anxiety The Solution Employment Hero partnered with Intellect to replace its reactive EAP with a complete mental health infrastructure built around the “Olympic Team” philosophy, the idea that elite athletes need expert coaching, adequate rest, and structured recovery to stay at their peak. – Proactive Coaching: Employees used Intellect for career planning and managing the psychological demands of high performance roles – Continuous Signal Detection: The Intellect Dimensions dashboard gave Employment Hero real time, aggregated data on presenting issues such as workload stress or anxiety – Choice of Formats: Same day or next day booking meant employees never had to wait weeks for support – Manager Capability: Managers were equipped with data driven webinars and conversation templates to lead informed wellbeing discussions during routine one-to-ones Results Just 90 days in, Employment Hero is seeing impact well beyond industry norms, proof that reframing support as performance optimisation, rather than crisis response, drives both adoption and genuine engagement. 22% Adoption Rate: Up from a 7% baseline and triple the Australian industry average 73% Repeat Users: Most employees who try Intellect return 4.89/5 Satisfaction Rating: Consistent high ratings across clinical and coaching sessions 9.2 Sessions per User/Month: Significant engagement compared to the typical three to five sessions
